items.title: Gauge invariance of hypermultiplet mass and adjoint couplings
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; the current N=1 vector-superfield interface is verified and the algebraic proof passes scoped checks.
items.statement:
Let $\mathscr R$ be the ring of even smooth chiral superfields on the specified flat superspace, with coefficients in the finite-dimensional supercommutative complex algebra of the superspace definition. Thus $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}f=0$ for $f\in\mathscr R$; its even elements commute. Fix an integer $n\geq1$, identify a specified based complex vector space $E$ with $\mathbb C^n$ and its dual with row vectors, and take $Q\in\mathscr R^n$, $\widetilde Q\in(\mathscr R^n)^*$ and $M\in M_n(\mathscr R)$. Suppose an invertible even chiral matrix $U\in GL_n(\mathscr R)$ acts by the explicitly supplied substitutions

$$Q'=UQ,\qquad \widetilde Q'=\widetilde Q U^{-1},\qquad M'=UMU^{-1}.$$

Then the chiral polynomials $\widetilde Q Q$ and $\widetilde Q M Q$ are invariant. In particular $\sqrt2\,\widetilde Q M Q+m\widetilde Q Q$ is invariant for every constant $m\in\mathbb C$. Assigning the formal degrees $[Q]=[\widetilde Q]=[M]=[m]=1$ makes this sum homogeneous of degree three. These are algebraic claims about the supplied action; they require no physical model or asserted supersymmetry realization. For the application $M=\rho_{R*}(\Phi)$, the same conclusion holds whenever that represented adjoint field has the stated conjugation law.
items.physical_scope: Pure algebra over the even chiral coefficient ring; no physical model, quantum measure or empirical premise is used.

items.title: Gauge invariance of the adjoint cubic superpotential
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current vector-superfield and pure Yang–Mills interfaces are verified and the proof passes scoped checks.
items.statement: Let $\mathscr R$ be the commutative ring of even smooth chiral superfields on the specified flat superspace, with the supercommutative complex coefficient algebra of the superspace definition. Let $\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3$ be traceless $2\times2$ matrices over $\mathscr R$. Use $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ and the complex-bilinear trace form $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, where $\operatorname{Tr}_2 A=\sum_{j=1}^2 A_{jj}$. Suppose a supplied invertible even chiral matrix $U\in GL_2(\mathscr R)$ acts simultaneously by $\Phi_i'=U\Phi_iU^{-1}$. Then the even chiral cubic polynomial $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi_1,[\Phi_2,\Phi_3])$ and every constant multiple are invariant. This includes the substitution $U=e^{i\Lambda}$ whenever the given even chiral parameter defines that invertible chiral matrix. The trace form restricts to the real form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on the explicitly defined real Lie algebra of anti-Hermitian traceless complex $2\times2$ matrices. No physical model, gauge measure or extended-supersymmetry premise is used.
items.physical_scope: Pure matrix algebra over the even chiral coefficient ring with a specified conjugation action and trace form; no physical premise is used.

items.title: Four-dimensional $N=2$ SU(2) vector and hypermultiplet model
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; all current formulation/model suppliers match the stated normalization; eight-supercharge invariance remains an adopted premise.
items.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Adopt a classical rigid four-dimensional model on the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing $x^0$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use $c=\hbar=1$. Fix $G=SU(2):=\{u\in M_2(\mathbb C):u^\dagger u=I_2,\det u=1\}$, not its quotient $SO(3)$. Its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(2):=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^\dagger=-X,\operatorname{Tr}_2X=0\}$, with adjoint action $\operatorname{Ad}_uX=uXu^{-1}$. The Pauli matrices are $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Choose one smooth right principal bundle $\pi:P\to M$ in the single sector $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$; its smooth right action is free and transitive on each fibre, it admits equivariant local trivializations, and $[P]$ denotes the nonempty minimum-rank set code of its smooth equivariant bundle-isomorphism type over $M$, in the supplied non-Abelian gauge-data convention. In the anti-Hermitian basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, use $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, so $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, and a fixed dimensionless coupling $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. Use $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^j:=\sigma_j$ for $j=1,2,3$, $\bar\sigma^0=I_2$, $\bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j$, and $\epsilon_{12}=1$; there is no theta term in this selected model.

Use the $N=1$ superspace algebra with even coordinates $x^\mu$ and odd coordinates $\theta^\alpha,\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$, the left derivatives and Berezin measures specified in the superspace definitions, and $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\theta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$, $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\theta^\beta\sigma^\mu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu$. A chiral field obeys $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi=0$. In each representation $R$, the dimensionless real vector prepotential $V_R$ transforms by $e^{2gV_R}\mapsto e^{i\Lambda_R^\dagger}e^{2gV_R}e^{-i\Lambda_R}$ and a chiral matter field transforms by $Q_R\mapsto e^{i\Lambda_R}Q_R$, where $\Lambda_R$ is a chiral gauge-parameter superfield. Its represented matrix curvature is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{-2gV_R}D_\alpha e^{2gV_R})$. Define $\operatorname{ad}(P)_{\mathbb C}:=(P\times\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C})/\sim$, where $[pu,X]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_uX]$. The connection-normalized vector multiplet consists on shell of the connection $A_\mu$, one complex adjoint scalar $\phi$ which is a smooth section of $\operatorname{ad}(P)_{\mathbb C}$, and two adjoint Weyl fermions; its $N=1$ decomposition is one vector superfield $V_{\mathrm{ad}}$ and one adjoint chiral superfield $\Phi$. The local representatives of $\phi$ obey $\phi_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}\phi_i$ when $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$. The canonical scalar is $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$. Here “on shell” means after eliminating algebraic auxiliary fields and imposing the field equations; the full vector superfield also contains the real auxiliary adjoint field $D$.

Choose a finite-dimensional complex vector space $\mathcal H_R$ with positive-definite Hermitian form $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_R$. A smooth unitary representation $\rho_R:SU(2)\to U(\mathcal H_R,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_R)$ means a smooth group homomorphism into the group of complex-linear isometries of this Hermitian form. Write $\rho_{R*}:\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal H_R)$ for the complex-linear extension of its differential at the identity. Its associated vector bundle is the quotient $E_R=P\times_{\rho_R}\mathcal H_R=(P\times \mathcal H_R)/\sim$, where $[pu,v]=[p,\rho_R(u)v]$ for $p\in P$, $u\in SU(2)$, and $v\in \mathcal H_R$. The hypermultiplet consists of chiral superfields $Q$ and $\widetilde Q$ whose scalar components are smooth sections of $E_R$ and its dual; the dual action is $\rho_{R^*}(u)\ell=\ell\circ\rho_R(u^{-1})$, and its Hermitian form is $\langle\ell_1,\ell_2\rangle_{R^*}=\sum_a\overline{\ell_1(e_a)}\ell_2(e_a)$ for any orthonormal basis $(e_a)$ of $\mathcal H_R$. For a local connection form $A_{\mu,\alpha}:U_\alpha\to\mathfrak{su}(2)$ from the selected Yang--Mills datum, the associated covariant derivatives on local scalar representatives are $D_\mu q_\alpha=\partial_\mu q_\alpha+\rho_{R*}(A_{\mu,\alpha})q_\alpha$ and $D_\mu\widetilde q_\alpha=\partial_\mu\widetilde q_\alpha+(\rho_{R^*})_*(A_{\mu,\alpha})\widetilde q_\alpha$, where $(\rho_{R^*})_*$ is the complex-linear extension of the differential of the stated dual action. Writing their left-Weyl components as $\psi_Q$ and $\psi_{\widetilde Q}$, the pair forms the Dirac field $\Psi_D=(\psi_Q,\overline{\psi_{\widetilde Q}})$, with both chiralities in $R$. Each chiral $N=1$ hypermultiplet field has one complex scalar, one Weyl fermion, and one auxiliary field; the pair therefore has two complex scalars, two Weyl fermions, and two auxiliary fields. Write $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}=\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ and let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be the complex-bilinear extension of $\kappa$. This form is nondegenerate and invariant under the complexified adjoint action, so for $R=\mathrm{ad}$ it identifies the dual with the adjoint. On the complexified adjoint define the Hermitian form $h_{\mathrm{ad}}(X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\overline X,Y)$, where conjugation is with respect to the real Lie algebra. The map $\jmath(X)(Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(X,Y)$ identifies this representation isometrically and equivariantly with its dual: in the $\kappa$-orthonormal basis $T_a$, $\langle\jmath(X),\jmath(Y)\rangle_{R^*}=h_{\mathrm{ad}}(X,Y)=\sum_a\overline{X^a}Y^a$, and invariance of $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ gives $\jmath(\operatorname{Ad}_uX)=\jmath(X)\circ\operatorname{Ad}_{u^{-1}}$. The local invariant pairing is $\widetilde Q Q$, and $\widetilde Q\Phi Q$ means $\widetilde Q\,\rho_{R*}(\Phi)Q$. Under a chiral supergauge transformation $U_R=e^{i\Lambda_R}$, use $Q\mapsto U_RQ$, $\widetilde Q\mapsto\widetilde Q U_R^{-1}$, and $M_R:=\rho_{R*}(\Phi)\mapsto U_RM_RU_R^{-1}$; the associated mass and cubic bilinears are gauge invariant. The hypermultiplet is canonically normalized, while $\Phi$ is in the connection normalization above. Write $\Phi=\sum_{a=1}^3\Phi^aT_a$; "holomorphic" means complex analytic in these complex coordinates on $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$, and $\partial_a$ denotes $\partial/\partial\Phi^a$. The microscopic vector prepotential is the holomorphic, gauge-invariant quadratic function

$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}(\Phi)=\frac{i}{2g^2}\,\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi,\Phi),\qquad \operatorname{Im}(\mathcal F_{ab})=\frac{1}{g^2}\kappa_{ab}>0.$$

Here $\mathcal F_{ab}=\partial_a\partial_b\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}$ in the basis $T_a$. With the normalized physical action brackets, its $N=1$ vector action is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{vec}}=\frac{1}{4g^2}\left([\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)+\frac{1}{g^2}[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi)]_D,$$

where $\mathcal W_\alpha$ is the abstract connection-normalized Lie-algebra-valued chiral curvature, with $\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}/(2i)$; hence its gauge F-term coefficient also equals $\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$ in the defining representation, before adding its Hermitian conjugate, and $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$. For a superspace expression $X$, $[X]_F=I_F(X)/2$ and $[X]_D=-I_D(X)/4$, using the raw generator order with the normalized physical brackets. Thus the vector kinetic term has exactly the connection-normalized Yang-Mills coefficient $-\kappa(F\wedge *_\eta F)/(2g^2)$.

The adopted renormalizable one-hypermultiplet action is

$$\mathcal L_{N=2}=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{vec}}+[Q^\dagger e^{2gV_R}Q+\widetilde Q^\dagger e^{2gV_{R^*}}\widetilde Q]_D+\left([\sqrt2\,\widetilde Q\Phi Q+m\widetilde Q Q]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right),$$

with complex mass parameter $m$ of dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$. In canonical normalization $\Phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\Phi/g$, the cubic coefficient is $\sqrt2g$, the same gauge coupling that appears in the covariant derivative. The ultraviolet prepotential above is quadratic; a low-energy effective prepotential may instead be non-polynomial and valid only on a specified electric/magnetic patch. This postulate adopts no such low-energy solution or duality claim.

The model includes rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetry: “rigid” means its spinor parameters are constant in spacetime, and $\mathcal N=2$ means two independent left-Weyl supercharges, hence eight real components. Its invariance is an adopted model premise, not a deduction in this item. The $N=1$ superspace expression is a field/action packaging; the full hypermultiplet transformations close only after imposing the physical field equations, and the finite $N=1$ auxiliary fields are eliminated in this on-shell description. Fields are smooth in local trivializations and admissible variations are smooth and compactly supported; actions are taken over relatively compact regions or when the spacetime integral converges. No path-integral measure, regulator, quantum theory, or continuum existence claim is included. In mass-dimension notation $[x]=-1$, $[\theta]=-\frac12$, $[\Phi]=[Q]=[\widetilde Q]=1$, $[\mathcal W_\alpha]=3/2$, $[m]=1$, and $[g]=0$; equivalently scalar fields and mass parameters have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$.

items.title: Four-dimensional $N=4$ SU(2) super-Yang-Mills model
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; current N=1/N=2/Yang–Mills interfaces match the adopted action; sixteen-supercharge invariance remains an adopted premise.
items.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing $x^0$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $P\to M$ be one smooth right-principal $SU(2)$ bundle, meaning its smooth right $SU(2)$ action is free and transitive on each fibre, it admits equivariant local trivializations, and its sector $[P]$ is the nonempty minimum-rank set code of its smooth equivariant bundle-isomorphism type over $M$, in the supplied non-Abelian gauge-data convention. The global group is $SU(2):=\{u\in M_2(\mathbb C):u^\dagger u=I_2,\det u=1\}$, not $SO(3)$; its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{su}(2):=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^\dagger=-X,\operatorname{Tr}_2X=0\}$ and its adjoint action is $\operatorname{Ad}_uX=uXu^{-1}$. The Pauli matrices are $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Use $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $c=\hbar=1$, and dimensionless coupling $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. Use $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^j:=\sigma_j$ for these spatial matrices, $\bar\sigma^0=I_2$, $\bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j$, and $\epsilon_{12}=1$, so $\sigma^\mu\bar\sigma^\nu+\sigma^\nu\bar\sigma^\mu=-2\eta^{\mu\nu}I_2$. Define the real adjoint bundle $\operatorname{ad}(P):=(P\times\mathfrak{su}(2))/\sim$ and its complexification $\operatorname{ad}(P)_{\mathbb C}:=(P\times\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C})/\sim$, both with relation $[pu,X]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_uX]$; the bar on $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$ is conjugation fixing $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. In the $N=1$ decomposition, $V_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is the dimensionless real adjoint vector prepotential with $e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\mapsto e^{i\Lambda^\dagger}e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}e^{-i\Lambda}$, where $\Lambda$ is a chiral gauge-parameter superfield, and $\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3$ are adjoint chiral superfields in connection normalization. Each $\Phi_i$ obeys $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$ and has one complex adjoint scalar, one adjoint Weyl fermion, and an algebraic auxiliary field. In the fixed physical chiral expansion write its scalar component as $\phi_i$, a smooth section of $\operatorname{ad}(P)_{\mathbb C}$ with local representatives $\phi_{r,\alpha}:U_\alpha\to\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$ obeying $\phi_{r,\beta}=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}}\phi_{r,\alpha}$ when local sections satisfy $s_\beta=s_\alpha g_{\alpha\beta}$. Define for $r=1,2,3$, with $\mathrm{i}^2=-1$

$$X^{2r-1}:=\frac{\phi_r+\overline{\phi_r}}{\sqrt2},\qquad X^{2r}:=\frac{\phi_r-\overline{\phi_r}}{\mathrm{i}\sqrt2},\qquad \phi_r=\frac{X^{2r-1}+\mathrm{i}X^{2r}}{\sqrt2}.$$

Thus each $X^I$ is a smooth section of $\operatorname{ad}(P)$, with local components transforming by $X^I_\beta=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}}X^I_\alpha$. The canonical chiral and real scalar fields are $\Phi_{i,\mathrm{can}}=\Phi_i/g$ and $X^I_{\mathrm{can}}=X^I/g$, respectively.


Write $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}=\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be the complex-bilinear extension of $\kappa$, set $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$, and write $[X,Y]$ for the complexified Lie bracket. The complexified form is nondegenerate and adjoint-invariant. For $U=e^{i\Lambda}$, each adjoint chiral field transforms by $\Phi_i\mapsto U\Phi_iU^{-1}$, so the adjoint cubic in the action is gauge invariant under this law. Use $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\theta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$ and $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\theta^\beta\sigma^\mu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu$. Each $\Phi_i$ is an even chiral superfield satisfying $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$, and the represented adjoint matrix curvature is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,\mathrm{ad}}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{-2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}D_\alpha e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}})$. The abstract connection-normalized chiral curvature in the action is $\mathcal W_\alpha$, defined by $\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}/(2i)$ for every representation $R$. Thus $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)/(4g^2)=\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$ in the defining representation, before adding its Hermitian conjugate. The adopted connection-normalized $N=1$ action is

$$\mathcal L_{N=4}=\frac{1}{g^2}\left\{\frac14\left([\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)+\sum_{i=1}^3[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi_i,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi_i)]_D+\left([\sqrt2\,\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi_1,[\Phi_2,\Phi_3])]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\}.$$

Here $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ and $[Z]_D=-I_D(Z)/4$ are the normalized physical brackets; the raw mathematical measures retain their coefficient-extraction meaning. In canonical fields, the cubic superpotential coefficient is $\sqrt2g$, so its Yukawa coupling equals the gauge coupling. On shell, meaning after eliminating algebraic auxiliary fields and imposing the field equations, the physical content is one gauge connection, six real adjoint scalars $X^I$ ($I=1,\ldots,6$), and four adjoint Weyl fermions $\lambda^A$ ($A=1,\ldots,4$). The scalar potential in connection normalization is

$$V_{\mathrm{scalar}}=\frac{1}{2g^2}\sum_{1\le I<J\le6}\kappa([X^I,X^J],[X^I,X^J]);$$

for canonical fields $X^I_{\mathrm{can}}=X^I/g$ this is $\frac{g^2}{2}\sum_{I<J}\kappa([X^I_{\mathrm{can}},X^J_{\mathrm{can}}],[X^I_{\mathrm{can}},X^J_{\mathrm{can}}])$. With the $N=2$ model's $N=1$ decomposition, this is the $R=\mathrm{ad}$, $m=0$ hypermultiplet specialization after rescaling its two canonical hypermultiplet chiral fields by $g$ to the connection normalization of $\Phi_2$ and $\Phi_3$.

Adopt rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetry, with four independent left-Weyl supercharges and sixteen real components, as part of this physical model postulate. The action's extended invariance and on-shell closure are not proved in this item. This is a classical action with smooth fields in local bundle trivializations and compactly supported admissible variations; no path-integral measure, regulator, quantum continuum theory, or empirical result is asserted. Use $c=\hbar=1$: $g$ is dimensionless, connection-normalized scalar fields have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and canonical fields have mass dimension one.

items.title: Gauge-invariant bilinears in one SU(2) hypermultiplet
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; generic and fundamental bilinear-invariance arguments pass under current supplier interfaces.
items.statement: Use the defining representation $R=\mathbb C^2$ with group homomorphism $\rho_{\mathrm{fund}}:SU(2)\to U(2)$ given by $\rho_{\mathrm{fund}}(u)=u$ acting by matrix multiplication. In each superspace fiber let $Q$ be a column in $R$, let $\widetilde Q$ be a row in $R^*$, and let $\Phi$ act by $\rho_{\mathrm{fund}*}(\Phi)$. Under any chiral supergauge transformation $U_R=e^{i\Lambda_R}$, set $Q'=U_RQ$, $\widetilde Q'=\widetilde Q U_R^{-1}$, and $\Phi'=U_R\Phi U_R^{-1}$. Then the mass bilinear $\widetilde Q Q$ and cubic bilinear $\widetilde Q\Phi Q$ in the adopted $N=2$ superpotential are gauge invariant. This checks gauge invariance of these two terms only; it does not prove the extended supersymmetry variation.
items.physical_scope: A local algebraic check of the mass and cubic superpotential terms in the classical N=2 SU(2) model for one fundamental hypermultiplet; it is not a quantum or empirical claim.

items.title: Constant gauge-coupling matrix from the quadratic $N=2$ prepotential
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; the Hessian and positivity calculation is complete for the adopted UV prepotential.
items.statement: For the adopted microscopic prepotential $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}(\Phi)=\frac{i}{2g^2}\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi,\Phi)$ with $g>0$ and $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, the Hessian $\mathcal F_{ab}=\partial_a\partial_b\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}$ is the constant matrix $i\delta_{ab}/g^2$. Its imaginary part is positive definite and independent of the scalar field $\Phi$. This is a property of the adopted quadratic ultraviolet model; it does not assert a non-polynomial low-energy prepotential.
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional calculation of the gauge-coupling Hessian in the adopted quadratic ultraviolet N=2 model; it does not establish an exact low-energy effective action.

items.title: $N=4$ action as a massless adjoint-hypermultiplet specialization
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; the conditional action and on-shell field-count comparison is proved.
items.statement: Set the $N=2$ hypermultiplet representation to $R=\mathrm{ad}$ on $\mathcal H_R=\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$, use $h_{\mathrm{ad}}(X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\overline X,Y)$ and the induced dual Hermitian form, and set its mass to $m=0$. The map $\jmath(X)(Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(X,Y)$ is an equivariant isometry from the adjoint representation to its dual, so it identifies $\widetilde Q$ with an adjoint field. If $Q$ and $\widetilde Q$ are the canonically normalized chiral fields, define connection-normalized adjoint chiral fields $\Phi_2=gQ$ and $\Phi_3=g\widetilde Q$; let $\Phi_1$ be the connection-normalized $N=2$ vector chiral field. Then the $N=2$ hypermultiplet kinetic terms and cubic superpotential become exactly the two additional adjoint-chiral terms in the adopted $N=4$ $N=1$ action, and the on-shell component counts agree: one vector, three complex adjoint scalars, and four adjoint Weyl fermions. The calculation does not prove the $N=4$ supersymmetry variation.
items.physical_scope: A conditional equality of the N=1 superspace action terms and on-shell field content for the N=4 SU(2) model and the massless-adjoint-hyper specialization of the adopted N=2 model; it does not prove sixteen-supercharge invariance.

items.title: Positive $N=4$ scalar potential for two noncommuting SU(2) fields
items.design_state: Step 1 ready; the explicit Pauli-matrix bracket and potential value are verified.
items.statement:
For real $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, take canonical adjoint scalar values $X^1_{\mathrm{can}}=aT_1$, $X^2_{\mathrm{can}}=bT_2$, and $X^I_{\mathrm{can}}=0$ for $I=3,4,5,6$, where $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and
$$\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
If $a,b\ne0$, the adopted $N=4$ scalar potential is $g^2a^2b^2/2>0$; if either coefficient is zero, it is zero.
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional classical field-value calculation in the adopted N=4 SU(2) scalar potential; it is not a field solution or empirical claim.
